module purpose: neorv32_cpu is a structural top level that wires a fetch frontend, a control unit, a register file, an ALU and a load/store unit, plus counter, PMP and ICC sub-units chosen by generics; locally it only bundles three request inputs (line 276), OR-merges extension CSR read data (line 279) and register write-back data (line 330), and ties the outputs of absent sub-units to constants (lines 305, 426-427, 454-455).

use-case flows.value: instruction fetch: the frontend sub-unit drives the instruction-bus request, takes its response and hands the fetched record to the control sub-unit
control bus driven by the control sub-unit into the frontend, counter, register-file, ALU, LSU and PMP sub-units, with four of its fields wired to the ICC sub-unit
register operands driven by the register-file sub-unit into the ALU, the control unit and (rs2) the LSU write-data input
register write-back data: ALU result, LSU read data, control CSR read data and ctrl.pc_ret OR-merged into rf_wdata and delivered to the register-file sub-unit
load/store access: the ALU sum delivered to the LSU address input with rs2 as write data; the LSU drives the data bus and returns read data
memory-protection check: the same ALU sum delivered to the PMP sub-unit, whose single-bit output reaches the LSU and the control unit; tied to '0' when RISCV_ISA_Smpmp is false
ALU and LSU status delivered to the control sub-unit (ALU 2-bit result and done bit; LSU wait, error and address-register values)
request bits from outside the CPU delivered to the control sub-unit (msi_i, mei_i, mti_i bundled; firq_i; dbi_i)
CSR read data of the counter, ALU, PMP and ICC sub-units OR-merged into xcsr_res and delivered to the control sub-unit; absent sub-units contribute zero
inter-core link: the ICC sub-unit drives icc_tx_o and reads icc_rx_i; icc_tx_o is tied to icc_terminate_c when ICC_EN is false

conceptual assets.concept: Memory-protection fault decision -- the single-bit result the PMP sub-unit computes for the load/store address and delivers to the LSU and the control unit
conceptual assets.reasoning: pmp_fault is driven by the PMP sub-unit through `fault_o => pmp_fault` (line 420, CONNECTS out at occurrence 4); that sub-unit receives the ALU sum as `addr_ls_i => alu_add` (line 418) and the control bus (line 414). The same bit enters the LSU (`pmp_fault_i => pmp_fault`, line 392) and the control unit (line 257). Both consumers are sub-units whose RTL is not supplied, so the boundary integrity property is Established from lines 257, 392 and 420: each must receive exactly the decision the PMP sub-unit drives. Configuration: the PMP sub-unit exists only when RISCV_ISA_Smpmp holds (line 402); otherwise `pmp_fault <= '0';` (line 427, constant driver at occurrence 5) so the decision never asserts in that build. alu_add is an operand of this decision, not its result, and is reported under its own concept. No line here restricts who observes the bit, so confidentiality is not established; no availability requirement is visible in this file.

conceptual assets.concept: Shared load/store address -- the ALU sum delivered both to the LSU as its access address and to the PMP sub-unit as the address it checks
conceptual assets.reasoning: alu_add is driven by `add_o => alu_add` (line 370, CONNECTS out at occurrence 3) and delivered unchanged to the LSU (`addr_i => alu_add`, line 386), the PMP sub-unit (`addr_ls_i => alu_add`, line 418) and the control unit (line 261). The RTL also establishes a consistency relation: the fault bit the LSU receives (line 392) is computed by the PMP sub-unit from the same signal the LSU receives at line 386; a value that differed between lines 386 and 418 would break it. conceptual assets.concept: Register write-back data -- the value delivered to the register-file sub-unit, merged from the ALU result, LSU read data, control CSR read data and ctrl.pc_ret
conceptual assets.reasoning: `rf_wdata <= alu_res or lsu_rdata or csr_rdata or ctrl.pc_ret;` (line 330, DERIVES_FROM at occurrence 3) computes the value delivered by `rd_i => rf_wdata` (line 323). The OR yields the intended value only while the sources not meant for a write are zero, so a corrupted source corrupts the written value. conceptual assets.reasoning: `xcsr_res <= xcsr_cnt or xcsr_alu or xcsr_pmp or xcsr_icc;` (line 279, DERIVES_FROM at occurrence 3) computes the value delivered by `xcsr_rdata_i => xcsr_res` (line 264).
